SELECTED_INDEX: 6
CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic features: two strong C-H stretches at 2937 / 2981 cm⁻¹, a single C=O band at 1719 cm⁻¹ and a group of CH₃/CH₂ deformation bands at 1458 / 1415 / 1357 cm⁻¹.  The mid-frequency region shows peaks at 1091 cm⁻¹ (C-O-C stretch of an ester) and at 952–857 cm⁻¹ (C–C–O bend and CH₃ rocking typical of aliphatic acetate esters).  
Candidate 6 (CCC(=O)OC(C)C, isopropyl acetate) contains one ester carbonyl and three alkyl CH₃ groups, exactly matching this pattern.  
Other candidates introduce functional groups whose characteristic Raman bands are absent: the nitro compound 1 should show a strong ν_as(NO₂) near 1530 cm⁻¹; compounds 3–5 have additional carbonyls expected to give a second C=O band, and 7, 9 lack any carbonyl.  
Thus the ester-only profile of candidate 6 best fits the observed peaks.
